title: Salesforce Admin
description: From your first org to the Administrator certification: data model, data quality, security and sharing, Sales and Service Cloud, page design, Flow and approvals, reports and dashboards, data tools, sandboxes and auditing.

nodes.title: Orgs, apps & Setup
nodes.summary: What an org is, how apps group your work, and where admins configure everything.
nodes.lesson:
An **org** is your company's instance of Salesforce: its data, configuration and users. To practise, use a free **Developer Edition** org: it doesn't expire. Companies test changes in **sandboxes** before touching **production**.

An **app** is a named set of tabs and items (Sales, Service, your own) that users switch between in the **App Launcher**. It's a view, not a separate database: every app reads the same records.

Admins work in **Setup** (the gear icon). Use the Quick Find box: type `Object Manager`, `Users`, `Flows`… and you'll rarely need to browse menus.

quiz.q: What is a Salesforce "app"?
options: A named set of tabs and items users open from the App Launcher
A managed package you must install
A separate database with its own records
quiz.why: Apps are navigation: groups of tabs over the same shared data.

quiz.q: Which org is free, doesn't expire, and is meant for learning and building?
quiz.why: Developer Edition orgs are free and permanent. Sandboxes are copies of a paid production org.

quiz.q: Where do admins configure objects, users and automation?
quiz.why: Setup (gear icon) is the admin's home; Quick Find gets you anywhere fast.

concepts: Production, sandboxes and Developer Edition orgs
Setup, Object Manager and the App Launcher
Licences, profiles and the difference between them
pitfalls: Changing configuration directly in production without testing it in a sandbox first.

nodes.title: Objects & fields
nodes.summary: Standard vs custom objects, field types, and formulas.
nodes.lesson:
An **object** is a table: Account, Contact, Opportunity are **standard** objects that ship with Salesforce. You create **custom** objects for your business; their API names end in `__c` (e.g. `Project__c`), and so do custom fields.

Pick field types deliberately:

- **Picklist** for a fixed list of values (clean reporting, unlike free text).
- **Formula** for a read-only value calculated from other fields every time it's read, e.g. `Amount * Probability`.
- **Lookup / Master-Detail** to relate records (next step).

Create objects and fields in **Setup → Object Manager**.

quiz.q: Custom object and custom field API names end in…
quiz.why: __c marks custom objects and fields. __r is a relationship name, __x an external object.

quiz.q: Which field type calculates a read-only value from other fields?
quiz.why: Formula fields are computed when read and can't be edited.

quiz.q: Which of these is a standard object?
quiz.why: Account ships with Salesforce; the others end in __c, so they're custom.

concepts: Standard and custom objects; custom ones end in __c
Field types and when to use each (picklist, formula, lookup, checkbox…)
Formula fields calculate on read and are never stored
pitfalls: Using a text field where a picklist would keep data consistent.
Building a formula when the value must be reported historically: formulas always show today's value.

nodes.title: Users & licenses
nodes.summary: Creating users, licenses, and deactivating instead of deleting.
nodes.lesson:
Every person who logs in is a **user** with a **user license** (which features they can ever use) and exactly one **profile** (their baseline permissions).

You can't delete users: you **deactivate** them, which frees the license and keeps the records they own and their history intact. If a deactivation is blocked (they're a default owner, for example), **freeze** the user first to stop logins immediately.

Username must be unique across *all* Salesforce orgs and look like an email address; the email field is where notifications go.

quiz.q: An employee leaves. What do you do with their user?
options: Change their profile to read-only and leave it active
Delete their records, then the user
Deactivate it (freeze first if you need to block login right away)
quiz.why: Users can't be deleted; deactivation frees the license and keeps data and history.

quiz.q: How many profiles does each user have?
options: As many as their role allows
quiz.why: One profile per user; extra access is added with permission sets.

quiz.q: A Salesforce username must be…
options: Unique across all Salesforce orgs, in email format
quiz.why: Usernames are globally unique and email-shaped, but don't have to be a real mailbox.

concepts: Profiles versus permission sets and permission set groups
Login hours, IP ranges and password policies
pitfalls: Deactivating a user who owns key automation or default lead routing: freeze them first.
Cloning profiles for every small difference: use permission sets.

nodes.title: Relationships
nodes.summary: Lookup vs master-detail, roll-ups and junction objects.
nodes.lesson:
- **Lookup**: a loose link. The child has its own owner and sharing; deleting the parent doesn't delete it.
- **Master-detail**: a tight link. The detail inherits the master's owner and sharing, can't exist without a master, and **is deleted with it**. Only the master can have **roll-up summary** fields (COUNT, SUM, MIN, MAX of details).
- **Many-to-many**: a **junction object** with two master-detail relationships, e.g. `Enrollment__c` between Student and Course.

quiz.q: In a master-detail relationship, what happens to detail records when the master is deleted?
options: Nothing; they keep a blank parent
They move to the default owner
quiz.why: Details can't exist without a master, so they're deleted with it.

quiz.q: Where can you create a roll-up summary field?
options: On the master object of a master-detail relationship
On either side of a lookup
quiz.why: Roll-ups summarise detail records onto their master.

quiz.q: How do you model many-to-many (students ↔ courses)?
options: A junction object with two master-detail relationships
quiz.why: Each junction record links one student to one course.

quiz.q: Look at the diagram. Which relationship would let Project__c show the total of its Expense__c amounts?
options: The master-detail from Expense__c to Project__c
quiz.why: Roll-up summary fields need a master-detail relationship, which Expense__c has to Project__c.
quiz.imageAlt: Relationships diagram: Expense__c is the detail side of a master-detail to Project__c.

concepts: Lookup versus master-detail, and what each means for deletion, sharing and roll-ups
Lookup filters to limit which records can be chosen
pitfalls: Converting lookup to master-detail when some records have no parent: the conversion fails.
nodes.diagramCaption: Lookup (Contact to Account), master-detail (Expense to Project) and a junction object (Enrollment) linking Students and Courses.

nodes.title: Validation rules
nodes.summary: Stop bad data at save time with formulas.
nodes.lesson:
A **validation rule** is a formula that describes *bad* data. When it evaluates to **TRUE**, the save is blocked and your error message is shown, at the top of the page or next to a field.

```
AND(
  ISPICKVAL(StageName, "Closed Won"),
  ISBLANK(NextStep)
)
```

Useful functions: `ISBLANK`, `ISPICKVAL`, `ISCHANGED`, `PRIORVALUE`, `REGEX`. Rules run on **every** save, from the UI, the API, imports and Apex, so they protect data everywhere, and can break integrations if you don't test them.

quiz.q: A validation rule blocks the save when its formula returns…
quiz.why: Write the formula to describe invalid data; TRUE means "block".

quiz.q: Which function checks whether a text field is empty?
quiz.why: ISBLANK is the recommended check for empty values.

quiz.q: Do validation rules apply to records saved through the API or Data Loader?
options: Only if the field is on the page layout
quiz.why: They run on every save regardless of where it comes from.

concepts: Validation rules that block bad data with a clear message
Required fields: on the field versus on the layout
Picklists and dependent picklists for consistent values
pitfalls: Making a field required on the field itself when only one process needs it: it blocks imports and integrations too.
Validation rules with unclear messages: users don't know what to fix.

nodes.title: Profiles & permission sets
nodes.summary: Object permissions, field-level security, least privilege.
nodes.lesson:
Two questions decide what someone can do:

1. **What** can they touch? **Object permissions** (Create, Read, Edit, Delete) and **field-level security** (visible / read-only). These come from the **profile** plus any **permission sets**.
2. **Which records**? That's **sharing** (next step).

Best practice: keep profiles minimal and grant extra access with **permission sets** (bundled into **permission set groups**). Adding is easy; taking away from a shared profile breaks other people.

quiz.q: A few users need to edit one extra field their profile can't. Best approach?
quiz.why: Permission sets add access to specific users without new profiles.

quiz.q: Field-level security controls…
options: Whether a user can see or edit a field
The order of fields on a page
quiz.why: FLS is per field: hidden, read-only or editable.

quiz.q: What do object permissions NOT control?
options: Whether you can read the object
Which specific records you can see
quiz.why: Which records is decided by sharing, not object permissions.

concepts: Permission sets and permission set groups
Session security, MFA and login access policies
pitfalls: Hiding a field only on the page layout: it's still in reports and the API.
Granting 'Modify All Data' to fix one access problem.

nodes.title: Record types & page layouts
nodes.summary: Different processes, picklists and layouts on one object.
nodes.lesson:
**Page layouts** arrange fields, related lists and buttons on a record. **Lightning App Builder** designs the whole record page; **Dynamic Forms** show fields only when they're relevant.

**Record types** let one object serve different processes: a *Partner* vs *Customer* Account can have different **picklist values** and **page layouts**, assigned by profile.

Careful: a field marked required **on a page layout** is enforced only in that UI. Make the field required in its definition (or use a validation rule) to enforce it everywhere.

quiz.q: What do record types let you vary for different processes on one object?
quiz.why: Record types drive picklist values and which layout users see.

quiz.q: A field is required on the page layout only. Is it required for Data Loader imports?
quiz.why: Use field-level required or a validation rule to enforce everywhere.

quiz.q: Which tool designs Lightning record pages with components?
quiz.why: App Builder lays out components; Dynamic Forms add field visibility rules.

concepts: Lightning App Builder record, home and app pages
Compact layouts, related lists and quick actions
pitfalls: Editing the page layout when the record page uses Dynamic Forms: the layout no longer controls those fields.

nodes.title: Automate with Flow
nodes.summary: Build real flows in your org, graded by tests.
nodes.lesson: **Flow** is the declarative automation tool (Workflow Rules and Process Builder are retired). Record-triggered flows that only update the triggering record should run **before save**: fast, no extra DML. Do the three problems below in your own org's Flow Builder; SFCode grades them with hidden tests.
concepts: Entry conditions and running only when a record changes to meet them
Where flows sit in the order of execution
Flow first, Apex when Flow can't
pitfalls: Updating the triggering record in an after-save flow: an extra save, and possible loops.
Using a Create or Update element inside a loop.
nodes.diagramCaption: Order of execution: before-save flows run before triggers and validation; after-save flows run after the record is saved.

nodes.title: Sharing: OWD, roles, rules
nodes.summary: Lock down with OWD, then open up.
nodes.lesson:
Record access is built in layers:

1. **Organization-wide defaults (OWD)**: the most restrictive baseline per object (Private, Public Read Only, Public Read/Write).
2. **Role hierarchy**: managers see what their team owns.
3. **Sharing rules**: open access to groups or roles by owner or criteria.
4. **Manual sharing** and **teams** for one-offs.

Everything after OWD only **opens** access; you can't use sharing rules to take it away. So set OWD to the strictest anyone needs, then open up.

quiz.q: What sets the baseline (most restrictive) record access for an object?
quiz.why: OWD is the floor; everything else opens access from there.

quiz.q: Can a sharing rule restrict access below the org-wide default?
options: No, sharing rules only grant extra access
quiz.why: Sharing only ever adds access.

quiz.q: OWD for Opportunity is Private. How does a sales manager see their team's deals?
quiz.why: Users above in the role hierarchy get access to records owned below them.

quiz.q: Look at the diagram. A user can't see a record. Which layer would you check first?
options: Organization-wide defaults, then whether a higher layer grants access
quiz.why: Start from the baseline and work up: the defaults, then role hierarchy, rules, manual shares.
quiz.imageAlt: Diagram of access layers with organization-wide defaults at the top.

concepts: Role hierarchy, owner- and criteria-based sharing rules
Public groups, queues and manual sharing
pitfalls: Setting OWD to Public Read/Write 'to be safe' and losing the ability to restrict later without rework.
Expecting a sharing rule to take access away: sharing only adds.
nodes.diagramCaption: Record access in layers: organization-wide defaults, role hierarchy, sharing rules, manual sharing and teams, and Apex managed sharing.

nodes.title: Reports & dashboards
nodes.summary: Report types, formats and dashboard running users.
nodes.lesson:
A **report type** decides which objects and fields a report can use (e.g. *Accounts with Contacts*). Formats:

- **Tabular**: a plain list.
- **Summary**: grouped by rows, with subtotals.
- **Matrix**: grouped by rows **and** columns.
- **Joined**: several report blocks side by side.

**Dashboards** visualise source reports. A standard dashboard shows data as its **running user** sees it; a **dynamic dashboard** uses each viewer's own access.

quiz.q: You need totals grouped by Stage (rows) and Close Month (columns). Which format?
quiz.why: Matrix groups by rows and columns.

quiz.q: What decides which objects and fields a report can include?
quiz.why: Report types define the available objects, relationships and fields.

quiz.q: Whose access determines what a standard (non-dynamic) dashboard shows?
quiz.why: Dynamic dashboards are the ones that use each viewer's access.

quiz.q: Look at the diagram. Which format shows several different report blocks side by side?
quiz.why: Joined reports combine blocks, each with its own report type and filters.
quiz.imageAlt: Diagram of four report formats: Tabular, Summary, Matrix and Joined.

concepts: Report types and what they include
Tabular, summary, matrix and joined formats
Filters, groupings, summary formulas and bucket fields
pitfalls: Using the standard report type when you need records without related records: build a custom report type ('with or without').
Saving reports in private folders, then wondering why nobody sees the dashboard.
nodes.diagramCaption: Report formats: Tabular is a plain list, Summary groups rows with subtotals, Matrix groups by rows and columns, Joined shows several blocks side by side.

nodes.title: SOQL for admins
nodes.summary: Query your data directly: filters and parent fields.
nodes.lesson: SOQL lets you ask precise questions of your data: in the Developer Console, in Flow "Get Records" thinking, and in tools like Data Loader exports. Try these two; they're graded against real records in your org.
concepts: Reading a SOQL query: SELECT, FROM, WHERE
Running queries in the Developer Console or a SOQL tool
Why admins use SOQL for data checks
pitfalls: Expecting SOQL to change data: it only reads.

nodes.title: Data import & tools
nodes.summary: Import Wizard vs Data Loader, duplicates, backups.
nodes.lesson:
- **Data Import Wizard** (in Setup): guided, up to **50,000** records, common standard objects and custom objects, with duplicate matching.
- **Data Loader** (desktop app): up to **5 million** records, any object, insert / update / upsert / delete / export, and can be scripted.
- **Duplicate rules** with **matching rules** warn about or block duplicates.
- **Data Export Service** schedules weekly or monthly CSV exports of your data as a backup.

quiz.q: You must load 1 million records. Which tool?
quiz.why: The Import Wizard tops out at 50,000; Data Loader handles millions.

quiz.q: Which feature warns about or blocks duplicate records?
quiz.why: Matching rules find duplicates; duplicate rules decide what to do.

quiz.q: Built-in way to schedule regular CSV backups of your data?
quiz.why: Data Export runs weekly or monthly exports.

concepts: Data Import Wizard versus Data Loader
Mass transfer, mass delete and the Recycle Bin
pitfalls: Importing without an external Id, then creating duplicates on the second run.
Leaving automation on during a large import: flows and triggers fire for every row.

nodes.title: Finding your way
nodes.summary: Apps, tabs, list views, search and Setup.
nodes.lesson:
Lightning Experience is organised into **apps** (Sales, Service, your own), each a set of **tabs** for objects and pages.

- **List views** filter and sort records; pin the one you use most. Kanban views show records by stage.
- **Global search** finds records across objects; **Setup** (the gear icon) holds every configuration screen, with Quick Find at the top.
- **Object Manager** is where objects, fields, layouts and record types are configured.
concepts: Apps, tabs and the App Launcher
Setup Quick Find and Object Manager
pitfalls: Creating dozens of public list views nobody uses: keep them curated.

quiz.q: Where do you configure an object's fields, layouts and record types?
quiz.why: Object Manager is the home of object configuration.

quiz.q: What shows Opportunities as cards grouped by stage?
quiz.why: Kanban views group records by a picklist such as Stage.

quiz.q: What groups tabs and pages for one kind of work?
quiz.why: Apps bundle the tabs and pages a role needs.

nodes.title: Company settings
nodes.summary: Company information, fiscal year, currencies and business hours.
nodes.lesson:
Org-wide settings shape everything else:

- **Company Information**: default locale, language, time zone and currency; licences in use.
- **Fiscal year**: standard (12 months from a chosen start month) or custom periods. It decides how `THIS_FISCAL_QUARTER` and forecasts work.
- **Currencies**: enable multiple currencies when you sell in several; each record then has its own currency, converted for reports.
- **Business hours** and **holidays** drive escalation rules, entitlements and SLA timers.
concepts: Company Information: locale, time zone, default currency
pitfalls: Enabling multiple currencies casually: it can't be turned off.
Forgetting business hours, so escalations count nights and weekends.

quiz.q: Where do you set the org's default time zone and see licences in use?
quiz.why: Company Information holds org defaults and licence counts.

quiz.q: Escalations should only count working time. What must be set up?
quiz.why: Escalation rules and entitlements count time against business hours.

quiz.q: What is true about enabling multiple currencies?
options: It can't be turned off once enabled
It can be turned off any time
quiz.why: Multi-currency is permanent, so plan before enabling it.

nodes.title: Record types and layouts
nodes.summary: Different processes on one object: record types, page layouts, picklists.
nodes.lesson:
**Record types** let one object serve different processes: *Hardware* and *Software* cases, *New Business* and *Renewal* opportunities.

- Each record type limits the **picklist values** available.
- **Page layout assignment** is by **profile and record type**: the same user sees a different layout per type.
- **Sales processes**, **support processes** and **lead processes** choose which Stage, Status or Lead Status values each record type uses.
- Users get record types through their profile or permission sets; one is their default.
concepts: When to use a record type (different process, values or layout)
Layout assignment by profile and record type
pitfalls: Creating record types just to show a different layout to different teams: Dynamic Forms or layout assignment by profile may be enough.
Adding a picklist value but forgetting to enable it on each record type.

quiz.q: Hardware and Software cases need different Status values. What do you configure?
options: Two support processes used by two Case record types
quiz.why: Support processes define the Status values; each record type uses one.

quiz.q: What decides which page layout a user sees?
options: The user's profile and the record's record type
quiz.why: Layouts are assigned per profile and record type.

quiz.q: You added a picklist value but users can't choose it on some records. Why?
options: It isn't enabled for those records' record type
quiz.why: Each record type has its own selection of picklist values.

nodes.title: Sales Cloud essentials
nodes.summary: Leads, conversion, opportunities, products and forecasting.
nodes.lesson:
The core sales flow:

1. **Leads** capture prospects, routed by **lead assignment rules** (including Web-to-Lead).
2. **Conversion** turns a qualified lead into an **Account**, a **Contact** and optionally an **Opportunity**, mapping lead fields to the new records.
3. **Opportunities** move through **stages**, each with a default probability and forecast category; **Path** guides reps through them.
4. **Products** and **price books**: a product needs a standard price before it can go in a custom price book; opportunity line items and quotes use them.
5. **Collaborative Forecasts** roll opportunity amounts up the role hierarchy.
concepts: Stages, probability, forecast categories and Path
Products, standard and custom price books
pitfalls: Custom lead fields not mapped for conversion: the data is lost.
Adding a product to a custom price book before giving it a standard price.
nodes.diagramCaption: Lead to cash: a Lead converts into an Account, a Contact and optionally an Opportunity, which gets a Quote with products and is closed.

quiz.q: Look at the diagram. Which record is optional when converting a lead?
options: None: all three are always created
quiz.why: Conversion always creates or merges an Account and a Contact; the Opportunity is optional.
quiz.imageAlt: Diagram: a Lead converts to Account, Contact and an Opportunity marked optional.

quiz.q: Using the diagram, where do the products on a Quote come from?
quiz.why: Products are priced through price books, then added to opportunities and quotes.
quiz.imageAlt: Diagram note: products come from price books.

quiz.q: Where is an opportunity stage's default probability set?
quiz.why: Each Stage value carries a default probability and forecast category.

quiz.q: Why can't a new product be added to a custom price book?
options: It has no standard price yet
It isn't active in a campaign
quiz.why: A product needs a standard price before any custom price book entry.

nodes.title: Service Cloud essentials
nodes.summary: Cases, queues, routing, escalation and Knowledge.
nodes.lesson:
- **Cases** come in through **Email-to-Case**, **Web-to-Case**, phone or chat.
- **Case assignment rules** route new cases to a user or **queue**; **Omni-Channel** pushes work to available agents by capacity and skill.
- **Escalation rules** act on cases still open after a time (counted in business hours): reassign, notify.
- **Auto-response rules** reply to the customer; **entitlements and milestones** track promised response times.
- **Knowledge** articles answer common questions; **macros** and **quick text** speed up agents.
pitfalls: Using assignment rules to escalate: they run on create and edit, not on time passing.
Escalation timings without business hours.
nodes.diagramCaption: Case lifecycle: Email-to-Case or Web-to-Case creates a case, an assignment rule routes it to a queue or agent, an escalation rule acts if it stays open too long, and it ends closed.

quiz.q: Look at the diagram. A case is still open after 8 hours. Which rule acts?
quiz.why: Escalation rules act on cases that meet criteria for a period of time.
quiz.imageAlt: Diagram: an Escalation rule box labelled 'still open after X hours', reached by a 'too slow' arrow.

quiz.q: Using the diagram, what routes a new case to a queue?
quiz.why: Case assignment rules route new cases to users or queues.
quiz.imageAlt: Diagram: Email-to-Case leads to an Assignment rule, then to a Queue / Omni-Channel.

quiz.q: What tracks whether first response happened within the contracted time?
quiz.why: Entitlement processes with milestones measure required steps against time.

nodes.title: More Flow
nodes.summary: Screen flows, scheduled paths, subflows and debugging.
nodes.lesson:
- **Screen flows** guide users step by step: on a record page, as a quick action, or in an app.
- **Scheduled paths** on record-triggered flows run actions relative to a date ("3 days before Close Date"); **scheduled flows** run on a timetable for a set of records.
- **Subflows** reuse logic across flows.
- **Fault paths** handle errors so users see a helpful message, not a crash.
- **Debug** runs a flow step by step with sample inputs; failed flow interviews email the admin.
concepts: Screen flows and where to launch them
pitfalls: No fault path: a single failure shows users an unhandled error.
A scheduled flow over a huge set of records without filters.
nodes.diagramCaption: Choosing automation: before-save flows for same-record updates, after-save flows for other records, screen flows to guide users, scheduled flows for timing, approval processes for sign-off, Apex when Flow can't.

quiz.q: Look at the diagram. Agents need a guided wizard to log a warranty claim. Which tool?
quiz.why: Screen flows show screens to users and collect input.
quiz.imageAlt: Diagram: 'Guide a user through steps' points to Screen flow.

quiz.q: Using the diagram, a manager must approve big discounts and the record must be locked meanwhile. Which tool?
quiz.why: Approval processes route for sign-off and lock the record.
quiz.imageAlt: Diagram: 'Someone must sign off, record locked' points to Approval process.

quiz.q: Send a reminder 3 days before an Opportunity's Close Date. What's best?
options: A scheduled path on a record-triggered flow
quiz.why: Scheduled paths run actions relative to a date field on the record.

quiz.q: What shows users a friendly message when a flow element fails?
quiz.why: Fault paths catch errors and let you handle them.

nodes.title: Approval processes
nodes.summary: Routing records for sign-off.
nodes.lesson:
An **approval process** routes a record to approvers when someone submits it:

- **Entry criteria** decide which records can be submitted (e.g. Discount over 20%).
- **Steps** name approvers: a specific user, the submitter's manager, a queue; steps can be sequential or require unanimous approval.
- **Actions** run on submit, approve, reject and recall: field updates, email alerts, tasks.
- Records are **locked** while pending; only admins and approvers can edit them.
- Flow's **Orchestrator** and approval actions can handle more complex multi-step work.
concepts: Initial, final approval, rejection and recall actions
pitfalls: No recall action, so a record stays locked if the submitter changes their mind.
Approvers who are inactive users: the request stalls.

quiz.q: What happens to a record while it's pending approval?
quiz.why: Pending records are locked; admins and approvers can still edit.

quiz.q: Which decides whether a record can be submitted at all?
quiz.why: Entry criteria filter which records qualify.

quiz.q: Where do you set a field to 'Approved' when the last approver approves?
quiz.why: Final approval actions run once the whole process is approved.

nodes.title: Dashboards
nodes.summary: Charts on reports, running users and snapshots.
nodes.lesson:
- Each **dashboard component** shows one source **report** (summary or matrix, or tabular with a row limit) as a chart, gauge, metric or table.
- The **running user** decides whose data appears. A **dynamic dashboard** runs as the person viewing it.
- **Dashboard filters** let viewers slice by a field; **subscriptions** email a snapshot on a schedule.
- **Reporting snapshots** copy report results into a custom object on a schedule, to trend data over time.
pitfalls: A dashboard running as an admin, showing everyone data they shouldn't see.
Source reports in private folders.

quiz.q: Each rep should see only their own data on one dashboard. What do you set?
options: The dashboard to run as the viewer (dynamic dashboard)
quiz.why: Dynamic dashboards run as whoever views them.

quiz.q: Leadership wants to see how the pipeline changed week by week. What captures history?
quiz.why: Reporting snapshots store report results on a schedule for trending.

quiz.q: What is a dashboard component's data source?
quiz.why: Every component is backed by a report.

nodes.title: Mobile and Chatter
nodes.summary: The Salesforce mobile app, quick actions and Chatter.
nodes.lesson:
- The **Salesforce mobile app** uses the same metadata as desktop: Lightning record pages, compact layouts and **quick actions**.
- **Quick actions** (log a call, create a related record, update fields) appear in the mobile action bar and on desktop.
- **Chatter** feeds let people follow records and colleagues, @mention others and post in groups. **Feed tracking** posts field changes to a record's feed.
concepts: Chatter feeds, groups and feed tracking
pitfalls: Designing pages only on desktop: test them in the mobile app too.

quiz.q: Field reps need a one-tap 'Log visit' on Accounts in the mobile app. What do you build?
options: An object-specific quick action on the Account layout
quiz.why: Quick actions show in the mobile action bar.

quiz.q: Followers of an Account should see a post when its Rating changes. What do you enable?
quiz.why: Feed tracking posts tracked field changes to the record feed.

quiz.q: Which fields does the mobile app highlight at the top of a record?
quiz.why: Compact layouts decide the key fields shown in the highlights.

nodes.title: Sandboxes and releases
nodes.summary: Building safely: sandbox types, change sets and release habits.
nodes.lesson:
Never build directly in production. Build in a **sandbox**, test, then move changes:

- **Change sets** send metadata between connected orgs: create an **outbound** change set in the sandbox, upload it, and deploy the **inbound** one in production. Deploying runs tests if Apex is included.
- Validate a change set before the release window; schedule releases when users are offline.
- Keep a release log; tell users what changed.
- Records aren't moved by change sets: plan data separately.
pitfalls: Forgetting dependent components (fields used on a layout, a flow's custom field) in the change set.
Building in a sandbox that's months behind production.
nodes.diagramCaption: Sandbox types: Developer and Developer Pro hold metadata only and refresh daily; Partial Copy adds sample data (5 GB, 5 days); Full copies all data (29 days).

quiz.q: Look at the diagram. You need to test with a realistic subset of production data, refreshed weekly. Which sandbox?
quiz.why: Partial Copy includes sample data chosen by a template and refreshes every 5 days.
quiz.imageAlt: Diagram: Partial Copy has metadata plus sample data, 5 GB, refresh every 5 days.

quiz.q: Using the diagram, how often can a Full sandbox be refreshed?
quiz.why: Full sandboxes copy everything and can be refreshed every 29 days.
quiz.imageAlt: Diagram: Full sandbox, refresh every 29 days.

quiz.q: What does a change set move?
quiz.why: Change sets carry configuration and code, never records.

nodes.title: Auditing and org health
nodes.summary: Who changed what: audit trail, field history and Health Check.
nodes.lesson:
- **Setup Audit Trail** lists configuration changes from the last 180 days: who, what, when.
- **Field history tracking** records old and new values for chosen fields (up to 20 per object); view it in the History related list or report on it.
- **Login History** shows who logged in, from where and how.
- **Health Check** scores your security settings against Salesforce's baseline and shows what to fix.
- **Optimizer** and **Security Center** (if licensed) highlight unused or risky configuration.
concepts: Field history tracking and its limits
pitfalls: Expecting field history to show changes from before tracking was turned on.
Ignoring Health Check findings because the score 'looks fine'.

quiz.q: Who changed the Opportunity sharing setting last week?
quiz.why: Setup Audit Trail records configuration changes.

quiz.q: You need old and new values of an Account's Rating over time. What do you enable?
quiz.why: Field history tracking stores before and after values.

quiz.q: Which tool scores your org's security settings against a baseline?
quiz.why: Health Check compares settings with Salesforce's recommended baseline.

nodes.title: Admin cert checkpoint
nodes.summary: Mixed scenario questions across the whole path.
nodes.lesson: The Admin exam is scenario-based: read what's asked, then pick the **least effort, most maintainable** declarative answer. Pass this checkpoint, then review any step you hesitated on.

quiz.q: Phone must be filled in only when Status is Closed. What do you build?
options: Make Phone required on the field
quiz.why: Conditional requirements are validation rules: AND(ISPICKVAL(Status, 'Closed'), ISBLANK(Phone)).

quiz.q: Support agents need Delete on Cases, but their profile is shared with others. Least-effort fix?
options: Give them the System Administrator profile
quiz.why: Permission sets add access to specific users without side effects.

quiz.q: Accounts must be Private, but the whole Finance team needs to read accounts in the Enterprise segment. What do you use?
quiz.why: Criteria-based sharing rules open access by field values to a group or role.

quiz.q: Each Course has many Students and each Student many Courses, and you need a count of students per course. What do you build?
options: A junction object with two master-detail relationships, plus a roll-up summary on Course
A lookup on Course and a formula
quiz.why: A junction object gives many-to-many; master-detail enables the roll-up count.
